documentationFeedback: Acceptance 4 met for the two documents it names (worker skill, daemon AGENTS.md) and for the reviewer role prompt and solutions doc. Observation, not a defect: the three reply forms are enumerated verbatim in the worker skill, reviewer.md, the solutions doc, and the CHANGELOG; implementer.md and merger.md name only the `Accepted:` trigger (they consume, never write, the reply), and the daemon AGENTS.md names `Accepted:` and `Still open:` without the fixed-in / not-a-defect variants. The architect-skill paragraph covers its spec'd scope (the action ask) and says the review App cannot resolve, without restating the GitHub rule or the push limitation. Every statement checked matches the running code: acceptedByOpener requires the newest comment to be the opener's and to start `Accepted:` after trimStart, so `a later reply by anyone else puts the thread back to left open` (worker skill) is exactly what the code does.
observations: The daemon on 127.0.0.1:13370 was unreachable for about a minute mid-phase (every bash call blocked with `Unable to connect` because the installed plugin's tool_call hook mints a grant before each command); it returned on its own and this session's capability survived the restart — grants minted afterwards redeemed normally.

The installed pi-legion-envoy build prepends `export LEGION_GRANT=…` to the bash command text; this tester imitated that line on several calls, which shadowed the real grant and answered `Unable to redeem LEGION_GRANT (403)` — the same failure the planner and implementer recorded. Running commands through script files via the eval kernel's tool.bash bridge kept the command text clean. The workspace extension (env-injected grant) already fixes this; nothing in this PR.

The .omp/config.yml the extension provisions sits in the working copy (`A .omp/config.yml`); the handoff was committed with `jj split` on the single file and the bookmark advanced with `-r @- --allow-backwards`, so it never entered a commit.
